title: Whistleblower protections gutted from the December 2023 NDAA

tellings.quote: and the Congress needs to enshrine in law, which they almost did in December of 23, a little over a year ago, but that got gutted in the reconciliation of the National Defense Authorization Act.

plain: The UFO activist Steven Greer says Congress almost wrote protections for UFO whistleblowers into law in December 2023, but they 'got gutted in the reconciliation' of the National Defense Authorization Act, the yearly defence law, which would mean lawmakers backed away from shielding insiders who come forward. The law signed on 22 December 2023, printed as Public Law 118-31 with a text nobody disputes, has the Archivist set up 'a collection of unidentified anomalous phenomena ... records in the National Archives' and lets release be postponed on 'clear and convincing evidence' of harm. The Senate's earlier UAP Disclosure Act had protected 'Witnesses, close observers, and whistleblowers providing information directly to the Review Board', an independent panel the final law does not set up, but Greer does not say which protections he means, and if they are these, the law shows where the talks between the House and Senate ended, not the bargaining that led there.

discussion.by: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024 (Public Law 118-31), sections 1841 to 1843
discussion.text: An act of Congress signed into law on 22 December 2023 and printed by the Government Publishing Office as Public Law 118-31; nothing about its text is disputed. The UAP sections of the law enacted on 22 December 2023 have the Archivist set up "a collection of unidentified anomalous phenomena ... records in the National Archives", have "each head of a Government office" identify and prepare such records for it, and let disclosure be postponed on the original classification authority's finding of "clear and convincing evidence" of harm. The Senate's UAP Disclosure Act of 2023 (SA 797) had given "Witnesses, close observers, and whistleblowers providing information directly to the Review Board" the protections of 50 U.S.C. 3373b(b) through an independent Review Board, and the enacted sections set up no such board; the teller does not say which protections he means, and if they are these, the law shows the end state of the conference he calls a reconciliation, not the bargaining that led to it.
